chapter: Miles Davis stories and what jazz means
title: The origin of the word jazz and what remains of it
summary: Gil says jazz originally meant pelvic action, then discusses what is left of jazz and when to use the word. A Bambi aside interrupts.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Jazz, the word jazz, originally before I ever heard the word jazz applied to music meant, pelvic action. Like you're jazzing. Jazzing, meaning you jazz. So it meant a pelvic motion so......
(Eric Partridge?) gives that kind of derivation in an entymological dictionary.
What it really means is a dance form in a sense. Do you know what I mean? Like a dance. We still have dances all the time, they just don't last as long as the word jazz does.
(Hudson Whittaker, typed Tight like that). Let's turn this off just a minute.

I Left my Baby' that's a beautiful one. So anyway jazz, that's the story, is a word. jazz as it were. And there's no use fighting about it. You use it when it's a good idea to use it and you don't use it when it isn't because it's going to go away and be replaced naturally anyway.
Well, the basic characteristics that still remain are what the syncopation and the improvisation is that it?

On your remaing jazz, there are, well there's the material of jazz and it's used a lot of times now in modern improvising which you can call jazz. But if it isn't called jazz, it still uses some of the material, comes in certain place with it then the rhythmic fixed beat stops and something else is going to be happening.
It's being used by composers now, you know. But the sum total is not jazz, it's a composition by a person.
Which uses some of the jazz element?

Yes. All groups that work, you know that you hear now are composers and make records that can be losely labeled jazz, they might not like to be called jazz or they may not even care because it doesn't really matter. It's the composition that matters.
And if it's nice to use it, if it brings a crowd, great, I think you should use it, if it doesn't don't.
